title: The quotient pullback tensor equation on flat-term K-flat complexes
statement: Fix a prime ell, a finite extension E of Q_ell and the actual integral and positive-power quotient coefficients R,S with reduction q:R to S [def-sfb-integral-quotient-coefficients]. Use internal module derived categories, their actual pullbacks L_R,L_S, scalar extensions D_T, scalar tensor isomorphisms b_T and the comparison lam:L_S D_Y isomorphic to D_X L_R, normalized by TensorNormalized and PullNormalized [lem-sfb-quotient-section-tensor-normalization]. For any scheme map f:X to Y and flat-term K-flat complexes P,Q of R_Y-modules [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], put U=Q_R(P) and V=Q_R(Q). Then lam_(U tensor V) followed by D_X(t_R(U,V)) and b_X(L_R U,L_R V) equals L_S(b_Y(U,V)) followed by t_S(D_Y U,D_Y V) and lam_U tensor lam_V, where t_R,t_S are the actual leftDerivedUpperStarTensor maps [def-sfb-module-object-projection-map]. This asserts equality on the given resolving models only; there is no flatness assumption on q, no boundedness assumption on P,Q, and no geometric hypothesis on f. The Lean index n:Nat denotes the positive exponent n+1.

proof.text: Use targetCompute_isIso and targetLocalization_isIso at P,Q. The latter is deduced from the given TensorNormalized b_X, without any exactness of quotient extension.

Apply left_flat_computation with b_X and PullNormalized lam, and right_flat_computation with b_Y and the same lam. Both normalize the corresponding derived path after the same targetCompute map; they have the same sourceCompute and inverse target localization.

Rewrite ordinaryLeft to ordinaryRight using the proved signed-total ordinary_square. Transitivity identifies the two derived paths after targetCompute. Cancel this invertible target map to obtain exactly the original displayed equation on Q(P),Q(Q).

theorem quotient_pullback_tensor_flat_model
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (E : Type u) [Field E]
    [Algebra (Padic l) E] [FiniteDimensional (Padic l) E] (n : ℕ)
    [∀ T : Scheme.{u}, HasDerivedCategory.{u + 1}
      (ModuleRingedComparison.modules (integral l E) T)]
    [∀ T : Scheme.{u}, HasDerivedCategory.{u + 1}
      (ModuleRingedComparison.modules (finite l E n) T)]
    (b : ∀ T : Scheme.{u}, TensorIso (reduction l E n) T)
    (_hb : ∀ T : Scheme.{u}, QuotientSectionTensor.TensorNormalized
      (reduction l E n) T (b T))
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (lam : D (reduction l E n) Y ⋙ L (finite l E n) f ≅
      L (integral l E) f ⋙ D (reduction l E n) X)
    (_hlam : PullNormalized (reduction l E n) f lam)
    (P Q : CochainComplex (Modules (integral l E) Y) ℤ)
    (_hP : (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso _ (.up ℤ)).kFlat P)
    (_hQ : (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso _ (.up ℤ)).kFlat Q)
    (_hPflat : ∀ i : ℤ, ObjectProperty.flat (P.X i))
    (_hQflat : ∀ i : ℤ, ObjectProperty.flat (Q.X i)) :
    lam.hom.app ((Functor.uncurry.obj
      (CondensedRing.derivedTensor (integral l E) Y)).obj
        (DerivedCategory.Q.obj P, DerivedCategory.Q.obj Q)) ≫
        (D (reduction l E n) X).map
          (((CondensedRing.leftDerivedUpperStarTensor (integral l E) f).app
            (DerivedCategory.Q.obj P)).app (DerivedCategory.Q.obj Q)) ≫
        (b X).hom.app ((L (integral l E) f).obj (DerivedCategory.Q.obj P),
          (L (integral l E) f).obj (DerivedCategory.Q.obj Q)) =
      (L (finite l E n) f).map
          ((b Y).hom.app (DerivedCategory.Q.obj P, DerivedCategory.Q.obj Q)) ≫
        ((CondensedRing.leftDerivedUpperStarTensor (finite l E n) f).app
          ((D (reduction l E n) Y).obj (DerivedCategory.Q.obj P))).app
            ((D (reduction l E n) Y).obj (DerivedCategory.Q.obj Q)) ≫
        (Functor.uncurry.obj (CondensedRing.derivedTensor (finite l E n) X)).map
          (Prod.mkHom (lam.hom.app (DerivedCategory.Q.obj P))
            (lam.hom.app (DerivedCategory.Q.obj Q)))
